notes:
disagreement: value: the case's final status: one pass requires closed_complete, the other awaiting_acceptance; chose closed_complete because the request names that state in words (resolved on that requirement).
disagreement: value: the three checklist items' descriptions: one pass tests the request's exact phrases, the other their key words; chose the key words because the request lists the steps unquoted, so their wording is not fixed (resolved on those requirements).
disagreement: disposition: HR case created for team transfer: one pass repaired it to closed_complete, the other kept its awaiting_acceptance; repaired because the request says 'close the case as complete' and the check's own description agrees.
The two passes otherwise agree on every requirement, row, id and cell, and on the other six dispositions (kept).
The benchmark's query tests awaiting_acceptance, which the policy reaches from closed_complete and which may be meant by 'propose this solution ... and wait for her approval'; the request names the closed state and asks for no move beyond it, so an agent that moves the case on to awaiting_acceptance fails the status requirement.
The knowledge link is narrowed from any article to New Hire Orientation, the only orientation or onboarding article in the seed.
The acting user, Karen Watkins, holds the admin role, which the policy says must not perform routine HR case work; the request and every benchmark check expect the work done.
The policy's closure constraint applies to mandatory tasks; the schema has no mandatory flag and the request does not say whether the task is mandatory, so the checklist task's own status is left untested.
The case short description (policy template, 30-120 characters) and the task's title and assignment are not fixed by the request and are left out.
